In [[algebraic group]] theory, a '''thin group''' is a discrete [[Zariski topology|Zariski-dense]] subgroup of ''G''('''R''') that has infinite covolume, where ''G'' is a [[semisimple algebraic group]] over the [[real number|reals]]. This is in contrast to a [[lattice (group)|lattice]], which is a discrete subgroup of finite covolume.

The theory of "group expansion" ([[expander graph]] properties of related [[Cayley graph]]s) for particular thin groups has been applied to arithmetic properties of [[Apollonian circles]] and in [[Zaremba's conjecture]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://gauss.math.yale.edu/~ho2/MSRI_Bourgain.pdf |title=Archived copy |accessdate=2014-07-24 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140729070337/http://gauss.math.yale.edu/~ho2/MSRI_Bourgain.pdf |archivedate=2014-07-29 }}</ref>
